title.zh: 卷一百一十七 載記第十七 姚興上
title.en: Volume 117 Records 17: Yao Xing Part One
title.raw: 卷一百一十七 載記第十七 姚興上 Volume 117 Records 17: Yao Xing Part One

sentences.zh: 姚興

translations.literal: Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Yao Xing.

translations.literal: (Part One)
translations.idiomatic: The first installment of the account.

sentences.zh: 姚興，字子略，萇之長子也。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, style name Zilüe, was Yao Chang's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, courtesy Zilüe, was the firstborn of Yao Chang.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時為太子舍人。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time he was a gentleman attendant at the heir apparent's palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he served as attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 萇之在馬牧，興自長安冒難奔萇，萇立為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Chang was at the horse pastures, Xing braved peril from Chang'an and fled to Chang; Chang established him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: While Yao Chang was raising troops in the pastures, Yao Xing slipped out of Chang'an through danger to join him and was named heir.

sentences.zh: 萇出征討，常留統後事。

translations.literal: Whenever Chang went out on campaign, he regularly left him behind to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang habitually left him in charge of the rear whenever he marched.

sentences.zh: 及鎮長安，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Chang'an, he had great awe-inspiring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As regent in Chang'an he combined stern authority with generous rule.

sentences.zh: 與其中舍人梁喜、洗馬範勖等講論經籍，不以兵難廢業，時人咸化之。

translations.literal: With his household gentleman Liang Xi, groom Fan Xu, and others he lectured and discussed the classics and records, and because of military hardship did not abandon study; people of the time were all transformed by it.
translations.idiomatic: With Liang Xi, Fan Xu, and other staff he kept debating the classics despite the war, and the capital gentry took his example.

sentences.zh: 萇死，興秘不發喪，以其叔父緒鎮安定，碩德鎮陰密，弟崇守長安。

translations.literal: When Chang died, Xing kept it secret and did not announce mourning; he had his uncle Xu garrison Anding, Shuo De garrison Yinmi, and his younger brother Chong defend Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing hid his father's death, posting Yao Xu at Anding, Yao Shuode at Yinmi, and his brother Yao Chong in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 碩德將佐言於碩德曰：「公威名宿重，部曲最強，今喪代之際，朝廷必相猜忌，非永安之道也。

translations.literal: Shuo De's generals and aides spoke to Shuo De, saying: "Your lordship's awe-inspiring name has long been weighty and your following is strongest; now at the juncture of the succession the court is sure to be mutually suspicious—this is not the way to lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode's officers warned him: "Your prestige and army outstrip everyone; at a moment of succession the throne will fear you—that is no way to stay safe.

sentences.zh: 宜奔秦州，觀望事勢。

translations.literal: You ought to flee to Qinzhou and watch how events develop.
translations.idiomatic: Flee to Qinzhou and wait on events.

sentences.zh: 」碩德曰：「太子志度寬明，必無疑阻。

translations.literal: " Shuo De said: "The crown prince's aims and measure are generous and clear; there will surely be no suspicion or obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: "Yao Shuode replied, "The heir is open-minded; he will not mistrust us.

sentences.zh: 今苻登未滅而自尋干戈，所謂追二袁之蹤，授首與人。

translations.literal: Now Fu Deng is not yet destroyed yet we seek arms among ourselves—this is what is called treading in the tracks of the two Yuans and handing our heads to another.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng still lives; civil war would repeat the Yuan brothers' folly and hand victory away.

sentences.zh: 吾死而已，終不若斯。

translations.literal: I would die first; to the end I will not be like this.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than do it.

sentences.zh: 」及至，興優禮而遣之。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, Xing treated him with generous courtesy and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported in, Yao Xing honored him richly and sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 興自稱大將軍，以尹緯為長史，狄伯支為司馬，率眾伐苻登。

translations.literal: Xing styled himself grand general, made Yin Wei chief clerk, Di Bozhi marshal, and led the host to attack Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing took the title grand general, appointed Yin Wei and Di Bozhi, and marched against Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 咸陽太守劉忌奴據避世堡以叛，興襲忌奴，擒之。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Xianyang Liu Jinu occupied Bishi Fort in rebellion; Xing raided Jinu and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jinu of Xianyang held Bishi fort in revolt; Yao Xing stormed it and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 苻登自六陌向廢橋，始平太守姚詳據馬嵬堡以距登。

translations.literal: Fu Deng from Liumo headed toward the ruined bridge; the Administrator of Shiping Yao Xiang held Mawei Fort to oppose Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng moved from Liumo toward the broken bridge while Yao Xiang of Shiping blocked him from Mawei fort.

sentences.zh: 登眾甚盛，興慮詳不能遏，乃自將精騎以迫登，遣尹緯領步卒赴詳。

translations.literal: Deng's host was very strong; Xing feared Xiang could not stop him, and personally led picked cavalry to press Deng, dispatching Yin Wei to lead foot soldiers to reinforce Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Fu Deng's numbers, Yao Xing rode out with elite horse and sent Yin Wei to reinforce Yao Xiang.

sentences.zh: 緯用詳計，據廢橋以抗登。

translations.literal: Wei employed Xiang's plan, occupied the ruined bridge, and resisted Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei followed Yao Xiang's advice and held the ruined bridge.

sentences.zh: 登因急攻緯，緯將出戰，興馳遣狄伯支謂緯曰：「兵法不戰而制人者，蓋為此也。

translations.literal: Deng thereupon urgently attacked Wei; Wei was about to go out to battle when Xing swiftly sent Di Bozhi to tell Wei: "The art of war's subduing others without fighting—this is what it is for.
translations.idiomatic: As Fu Deng stormed Yin Wei's line, Yao Xing sent Di Bozhi with a warning: "The sage general wins without fighting—this is such a case.

sentences.zh: 苻登窮寇，宜持重，不可輕戰。

translations.literal: Fu Deng is a cornered bandit; you ought to hold firm and not fight lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng is desperate; stand fast and do not risk a rash clash.

sentences.zh: 」緯曰：「先帝登遐，人情擾懼，今不因思奮之力，梟殄逆豎，大事去矣。

translations.literal: " Wei said: "The late emperor has ascended far; human hearts are disturbed and fearful; now if we do not rely on the power of thinking of him and striving, beheading and destroying the rebellious stripling, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: "Yin Wei answered, "The late king has just died and morale wavers; if we do not strike now and crush Fu Deng, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 緯敢以死爭。

translations.literal: Wei dares to dispute this with death.
translations.idiomatic: I will stake my life on this.

sentences.zh: 」遂與登戰，大破之，登眾渴死者十二三，其夜大潰，登奔雍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he fought Deng, greatly defeated him; twelve or thirteen parts of Deng's host died of thirst; that night they greatly scattered; Deng fled to Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He gave battle, shattered Fu Deng, and left two-thirds of the enemy dying of thirst; that night Fu Deng's army melted away and he fled to Yong.

sentences.zh: 興乃發喪行服。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon announced mourning and observed the rites of bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yao Xing proclaim his father's death and don mourning.

sentences.zh: 太元十九年，僭即帝位於槐里，大赦境內，改元曰皇初，遂如安定。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan he unlawfully assumed the imperial dignity at Huaili, granted a general amnesty within his borders, changed the era name to Huangchu, and proceeded to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 19 he declared himself emperor at Huaili, amnestied his realm, took the reign name Huangchu, and moved to Anding.

sentences.zh: 先是，苻登使弟廣守雍，子崇屯胡空堡，聞登敗，各棄守走。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fu Deng had ordered his younger brother Guang to guard Yong and his son Chong to encamp at Hu Kong's Fort; hearing Deng was defeated, each abandoned defense and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng had left Fu Guang at Yong and crown prince Fu Chong at Hu Kong; both bolted when they heard of his defeat.

sentences.zh: 登無所投據，遂奔平涼，率其餘眾入馬毛山。

translations.literal: Deng had nowhere to cast anchor; thereupon he fled to Pingliang, led his remaining host into Maomao Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng retreated to Pingliang and climbed Maomao Mountain with his survivors.

sentences.zh: 興自安定如涇陽，與登戰于山南，斬登。

translations.literal: Xing from Anding went to Jingyang, fought Deng south of the mountain, and beheaded Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing advanced from Anding to Jingyang and slew Fu Deng south of the range.

sentences.zh: 散其部眾，歸復農業。

translations.literal: He scattered Deng's following and returned them to agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He disbanded Fu Deng's troops to the plow.

sentences.zh: 徙陰密三萬戶于長安，分大營戶為四，置四軍以領之。

translations.literal: He moved thirty thousand households of Yinmi to Chang'an, divided the great camp households into four, and set up four armies to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled thirty thousand Yinmi households in Chang'an, split the great camp into four armies, and assigned commanders.

sentences.zh: 安南強熙、鎮遠楊多叛，推竇沖為盟主，所在擾亂。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the South Qiang Xi and Yang Duo, general who guards the distance, rebelled, raised Dou Chong as covenant lord, and everywhere disturbed and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi, general who pacifies the south, and Yang Duo rebelled, made Dou Chong their leader, and stirred the region.

sentences.zh: 興率諸將討之，軍次武功，多兄子良國殺多而降。

translations.literal: Xing led the generals to punish them; the army halted at Wugong; Duo's elder brother's son Liangguo killed Duo and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched to suppress them; at Wugong Yang Duo's nephew Liangguo killed him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 沖弟彰武與沖離貳，沖奔強熙。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhangwu broke with Chong; Chong fled to Qiang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong's brother Zhangwu turned on him, and Dou Chong fled to Qiang Xi.

sentences.zh: 熙聞興將至，率戶二千奔秦州。

translations.literal: Xi, hearing Xing was about to arrive, led two thousand households in flight to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi took two thousand households to Qinzhou when he learned Yao Xing was coming.

sentences.zh: 竇沖走汧川，汧川氐仇高執送之。

translations.literal: Dou Chong fled to Qian River; the Di of Qian River Qiu Gao seized him and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chong ran to the Qian valley; the Di chief Qiu Gao seized him and handed him over.

sentences.zh: 沖從弟統率其眾降於興。

translations.literal: Chong's younger cousin Tong led his host to surrender to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tong, Dou Chong's cousin, brought his men to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 封征虜緒為晉王，征西碩德為隴西王，征南靖等及功臣尹緯、齊難、楊佛嵩等並為公侯，其餘封爵各有差。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the General Who Conquers Barbarians Xu as Prince of Jin, the General Who Conquers the West Shuo De as Prince of Longxi, the General Who Conquers the South Jing and others together with meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others all as dukes or marquises; the remaining enfeoffments each had their gradations.
translations.idiomatic: He made Yao Xu prince of Jin, Yao Shuode prince of Longxi, and ennobled Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and other generals as dukes or marquises.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑薛勃於貳城為魏軍所伐，遣使請救，使姚崇赴救。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo at Ercheng was attacked by Wei troops and sent envoys begging rescue; he sent Yao Chong to hurry to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Xue Bo at Ercheng, Yao Xing sent Yao Chong to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 魏師既還，薛勃復叛，崇伐而執之，大收其士馬而還。

translations.literal: After the Wei army returned, Xue Bo rebelled again; Chong attacked and seized him, greatly collected his soldiers and horses, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei withdrew, Xue Bo rebelled again; Yao Chong captured him and drove off his herds.

sentences.zh: 興追尊其庶母孫氏為皇太后，配饗太廟。

translations.literal: Xing posthumously honored his concubine mother Lady Sun as empress dowager and paired her for sacrifice in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously titled his stepmother Sun empress dowager and enshrined her with the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 楊盛保仇池，遣使請命，拜使持節、鎮南將軍、仇池公。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng held Qiuqi and sent envoys begging appointment; he was appointed Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Qiuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng of Qiuqi submitted and received tally, general who guards the south, and duke of Qiuqi.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑越質詰歸率戶二萬叛乞伏乾歸，降於興，興處之于成紀，拜使持節、鎮西將軍、平襄公。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Yuezhi Jiegui led twenty thousand households in revolt from Qifu Gangui and surrendered to Xing; Xing settled them at Chengji and appointed him Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, General Who Guards the West, and Duke of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi Jiegui brought twenty thousand households from Qifu Gangui to Yao Xing, who settled them at Chengji and titled him general who guards the west, duke of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 姚碩德討平涼胡金豹於洛城，克之。

translations.literal: Yao Shuode attacked and punished the Pingliang Hu Jin Bao at Luocheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode crushed the Pingliang Hu Jin Bao at Luocheng.

sentences.zh: 初，上邽薑乳據本縣以叛，自稱秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiang Ru of Shanggui had held his home county in rebellion and styled himself Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ru of Shanggui had seized his county and called himself inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 碩德進討之，乳率眾降。

translations.literal: Shuo De advanced to punish him; Ru led the host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode marched in; Jiang Ru surrendered.

sentences.zh: 以碩德為秦州牧，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: He made Shuo De Governor of Qinzhou, concurrently Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, and garrisoned Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yao Shuode governor of Qinzhou and colonel of the eastern Qiang at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 征乳為尚書。

translations.literal: He summoned Ru to be Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ru was summoned to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 強熙及略陽豪族權幹城率眾三萬圍上邽，碩德擊破之。

translations.literal: Qiang Xi and Quan Gancheng of the magnate clans of Lüeyang led thirty thousand to besiege Shanggui; Shuo De broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi and Lüeyang magnate Quan Gancheng besieged Shanggui with thirty thousand men until Yao Shuode routed them.

sentences.zh: 熙南奔仇池，遂假道歸晉。

translations.literal: Xi fled south to Qiuqi, thereupon borrowed a road and returned to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xi ran to Qiuqi and then passed through to Jin.

sentences.zh: 碩德西討幹城，幹城降。

translations.literal: Shuo De campaigned west against Gancheng; Gancheng surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode marched west; Quan Gancheng yielded.

sentences.zh: 興令郡國各歲貢清行孝廉一人。

translations.literal: Xing ordered each commandery and princedom annually to present one man of pure conduct recommended as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing required every district to recommend one filial, incorrupt candidate each year.

sentences.zh: 慕容永既為慕容垂所滅，河東太守柳恭等各阻兵自守，興遣姚緒討之。

translations.literal: After Murong Yong had been destroyed by Murong Chui, the Administrator of Hedong Liu Gong and others each blocked arms and guarded themselves; Xing sent Yao Xu to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yong fell, Liu Gong of Hedong and others held out until Yao Xing sent Yao Xu.

sentences.zh: 恭等依河距守，緒不得濟。

translations.literal: Gong and others relied on the river to hold defense; Xu could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong barred the Yellow River; Yao Xu could not ford.

sentences.zh: 鎮東薛強先據楊氏壁，引緒從龍門濟河，遂入蒲阪。

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the East Xue Qiang first held Yang's fort, led Xu from Longmen to cross the river, and thereupon entered Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qiang held Yang's redoubt and guided Yao Xu across at Longmen into Puyang.

sentences.zh: 恭勢屈，請降。

translations.literal: Gong's power was bent; he begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gong submitted when outflanked.

sentences.zh: 徙新平、安定新戶六千于蒲阪。

translations.literal: He moved six thousand new households of Xinping and Anding to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand households from Xinping and Anding were resettled at Puban.

sentences.zh: 興母虵氏死，興哀毀過禮，不親庶政。

translations.literal: Xing's mother Lady She died; Xing's grief destroyed him beyond the rites and he did not personally attend to miscellaneous government.
translations.idiomatic: Lady She died; Yao Xing mourned past all measure and ignored routine state business.

sentences.zh: 群臣議請依漢、魏故事，既葬即吉。

translations.literal: The host of ministers debated and asked to follow Han and Wei precedent—after burial then observe auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers urged Han and Wei practice: end mourning at burial.

sentences.zh: 興尚書郎李嵩上疏曰「三王異制，五帝殊禮。

translations.literal: Xing's Gentleman of the Secretariat Li Song submitted a memorial, saying: "The three kings had differing institutions, the five emperors had diverse rites.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song argued that the three kings and five emperors kept different mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 孝治天下，先王之高事也，宜遵聖性，以光道訓。

translations.literal: Filial piety governing the realm is the high affair of former kings; it is fitting to follow sagely nature to brighten the way's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Filial rule is the hallmark of sage-kings; the emperor should follow his heart to teach the realm.

sentences.zh: 既葬之後，應素服臨朝，率先天下，仁孝之舉也。

translations.literal: After burial, he ought to attend court in plain white, taking the lead under heaven—an act of benevolent filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he should hold court in undyed hemp to show the empire how a son grieves.

sentences.zh: 」尹緯駁曰：「帝王喪制，漢、魏為准。

translations.literal: " Yin Wei refuted, saying: "Imperial mourning regulations take Han and Wei as standard.
translations.idiomatic: "Yin Wei countered that Han and Wei set the court precedent.

sentences.zh: 嵩矯常越禮，愆於軌度，請付有司，以專擅論。

translations.literal: Song bends the constant and leaps the rites, errs against measure; I ask he be handed to the responsible office and judged for usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song twists custom; hand him to the judges for overstepping.

sentences.zh: 既葬即吉，乞依前議。

translations.literal: After burial observe auspicious rites; I beg to follow the prior discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Bury the empress dowager, then end mourning as we first proposed.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「嵩忠臣孝子，有何咎乎？

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Song is a loyal minister and filial son—what fault has he?
translations.idiomatic: "Yao Xing said, "Li Song is loyal and filial—what crime is that?

sentences.zh: 尹僕射棄先王之典，而欲遵漢、魏之權制，豈所望於朝賢哉！

translations.literal: Director Yin discards the former kings' canon and wishes to follow Han and Wei's expedient system—is this what is hoped from the court's worthies!
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei would toss the classics for Han expediency—is that what we expect of ministers?

sentences.zh: 其一依嵩議。」

translations.literal: Let it all first follow Song's discussion."
translations.idiomatic: We will follow Li Song's advice."

sentences.zh: 鮮卑薛勃叛奔嶺北，上郡、貳川雜胡皆應之，遂圍安遠將軍姚詳于金城。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Xue Bo rebelled and fled north of the ranges; the miscellaneous Hu of Shang commandery and Ercheng all answered him, thereupon besieging the General Who Pacifies the Distance Yao Xiang at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo fled beyond the passes; Hu of Shang and Ercheng joined him and besieged Yao Xiang at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 遣姚崇、尹緯討之。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Chong and Yin Wei to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Yao Chong and Yin Wei.

sentences.zh: 勃自三交趣金城，崇列營掎之，而租運不繼，三軍大饑。

translations.literal: Bo from Sanjiao hastened toward Jincheng; Chong set camps to check him, but transport of grain did not continue and the three armies were greatly hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo raced from Sanjiao; Yao Chong checked him but supplies failed and the army starved.

sentences.zh: 緯言於崇曰：「輔國彌姐高地、建節杜成等皆諸部之豪，位班三品，督運稽留，令三軍乏絕，宜明置刑書，以懲不肅。

translations.literal: Wei spoke to Chong, saying: "The State-Supporting Mizhi Gaodi, the Lineage-Establishing Du Cheng, and others are all magnates of the various divisions, ranked third grade, supervising transport yet delaying—making the three armies lack supplies—it is fitting clearly to set penal texts to punish lack of discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Wei told Yao Chong to execute Mizhi Gaodi, Du Cheng, and other nobles who had stalled the grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: They were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 諸部大震，租入者五十餘萬。

translations.literal: The various divisions were greatly shaken; those who rendered grain exceeded five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The clans panicked and forwarded over five hundred thousand measures of grain.

sentences.zh: 興率步騎二萬親討之，勃懼，棄其眾奔于高平公沒奕于，於執而送之。

translations.literal: Xing led twenty thousand foot and horse personally to punish him; Bo feared, abandoned his host, and fled to Duke of Gaoping Moyuyu, who seized him and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing took twenty thousand men against Xue Bo, who abandoned his troops and fled to Moyuyu of Gaoping; Moyuyu seized him and sent him in.

sentences.zh: 泫氏男姚買得欲因興葬母虵氏殺興，會有告之者，興未之信，遣李嵩詐往。

translations.literal: The baron of Xuan county Yao Maide wished to take advantage of Xing burying his mother Lady She to kill Xing; it happened that there was one who informed him, yet Xing did not believe it and sent Li Song feigning another purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Maide plotted to strike during Lady She's funeral; when a tip came, Yao Xing doubted it and sent Li Song to probe.

sentences.zh: 買得具以告嵩，嵩還，以聞，興乃賜買得死，誅其黨與。

translations.literal: Maide fully told Song; Song returned and reported; Xing thereupon granted Maide death and executed his accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Maide confessed to Li Song; Yao Xing ordered his death and purged his party.

sentences.zh: 興下書禁百姓造錦繡及淫祀。

translations.literal: Xing issued a document forbidding the hundred surnames to make brocade embroidery and excessive sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He banned commoners from weaving fancy silks and from illicit shrines.

sentences.zh: 興率眾寇湖城，晉弘農太守陶仲山、華山太守董邁皆降於興。

translations.literal: Xing led the host to raid Hucheng; Jin's Administrator of Hongnong Tao Zhongshan and Administrator of Huashan Dong Mai both surrendered to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Hucheng; Tao Zhongshan and Dong Mai of Jin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂如陝城，進寇上洛，陷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Shancheng, advanced to raid Shangluo, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He took Shancheng and Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 遣姚崇寇洛陽，晉河南太守夏侯宗之固守金墉，崇攻之不克，乃陷柏穀，徙流人西河嚴彥、河東裴岐、韓襲等二萬餘戶而還。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Chong to raid Luoyang; Jin's Administrator of Henan Xiahou Zongzhi stubbornly defended Jinyong; Chong attacked but could not take it, thereupon captured Baigu, moved more than twenty thousand refugee households of Xihe Yan Yan, Hedong Pei Qi, Han Xi, and others, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong failed at Jinyong against Xiahou Zongzhi but sacked Baigu and deported twenty thousand refugee families.

sentences.zh: 興下書，令士卒戰亡者守宰所在埋藏之，求其近親為之立後。

translations.literal: Xing issued a document ordering that soldiers who died in battle be buried where they fell by the local magistrate, and their close kin be sought to establish heirs for them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered battlefield dead buried locally and heirs found for each soldier.

sentences.zh: 武都氐屠飛、啖鐵等殺隴東太守姚回，略三千餘家，據方山以叛。

translations.literal: The Di of Wudu Tu Fei, Dan Tie, and others killed the Administrator of Longdong Yao Hui, plundered more than three thousand households, and held Fangshan in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Wudu Di Tu Fei and Dan Tie slew Yao Hui, seized three thousand families, and held Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 興遣姚紹等討之，斬飛、鐵。

translations.literal: Xing sent Yao Shao and others to punish them, beheading Fei and Tie.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao executed Tu Fei and Dan Tie.

sentences.zh: 遣狄伯支迎流人曹會、牛壽萬餘戶於漢中。

translations.literal: He sent Di Bozhi to welcome more than ten thousand refugee households of Cao Hui and Niu Shou from Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Di Bozhi escorted ten thousand refugees from Hanzhong led by Cao Hui and Niu Shou.

sentences.zh: 興留心政事，苞容廣納，一言之善，咸見禮異。

translations.literal: Xing attended to government affairs, was tolerant and broadly receptive; if a single word was good, all were treated with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing governed attentively and welcomed counsel; sound advice won favor.

sentences.zh: 京兆杜瑾、馮翊吉默、始平周寶等上陳時事，皆擢處美官。

translations.literal: Du Jin of Jingzhao, Ji Mo of Fengyi, Zhou Bao of Shiping, and others submitted memorials on current affairs and were all promoted to fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jin, Ji Mo, Zhou Bao, and others who wrote on policy won high posts.

sentences.zh: 天水姜龕、東平淳于岐、馮翊郭高等皆耆儒碩德，經明行修，各門徒數百，教授長安，諸生自遠而至者萬數千人。

translations.literal: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Gao Guo of Fengyi, and others were all aged Confucians of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, each with several hundred disciples, teaching in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Elder scholars such as Jiang Kan, Chunyu Qi, and Gao Guo taught thousands of students in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 興每於聽政之暇，引龕等於東堂，講論道藝，錯綜名理。

translations.literal: Whenever Xing in the leisure of hearing government led Kan and others into the east hall, they lectured and discussed the way and arts, interweaving names and principles.
translations.idiomatic: Between audiences Yao Xing debated metaphysics with them in the east hall.

sentences.zh: 涼州胡辯，苻堅之末，東徙洛陽，講授弟子千有餘人，關中後進多赴之請業。

translations.literal: Hu Bian of Liangzhou, at the end of Fu Jian's time, moved east to Luoyang and lectured to more than a thousand disciples; many later students of Guanzhong went to him to seek instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Bian of Liangzhou had fled to Luoyang with a thousand pupils; Guanzhong students flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 興敕關尉曰：「諸生諮訪道藝，修己厲身，往來出入，勿拘常限。

translations.literal: Xing ordered the pass commandant: "Gentlemen who inquire into the way and arts, cultivate themselves and toughen their persons, coming and going in and out—do not restrain them with ordinary limits.
translations.idiomatic: He told the gate wardens not to hinder scholars traveling for study.

sentences.zh: 」於是學者咸勸，儒風盛焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon scholars were all encouraged, and Confucian wind flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Learning flourished and Confucian study spread.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎古成詵、中書侍郎王尚、尚書郎馬岱等，以文章雅正，參管機密。

translations.literal: Gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Gucheng Shen, palace attendant Wang Shang, gentleman of the secretariat Ma Dai, and others, because their literary compositions were elegant and correct, participated in managing secret matters.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen, Wang Shang, Ma Dai, and others of polished prose joined the privy council.

sentences.zh: 詵風韻秀舉，確然不群，每以天下是非為己任。

translations.literal: Shen's bearing was elegant and outstanding, firm and not of the crowd; he always took the realm's right and wrong as his own task.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen carried himself like a lone crane and made the kingdom's conscience his business.

sentences.zh: 時京兆韋高慕阮籍之為人，居母喪，彈琴飲酒。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Gao of Jingzhao admired Ruan Ji's conduct; dwelling in mourning for his mother, he played zither and drank wine.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao of Jingzhao aped Ruan Ji, playing music and drinking during his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 詵聞而泣曰：「吾當私刃斬之，以崇風教。

translations.literal: Shen heard and wept, saying: "I ought to kill him with a private blade to exalt custom and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen swore to cut him down for the sake of public morals.

sentences.zh: 」遂持劍求高。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took a sword and sought Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a sword and hunted Wei Gao.

sentences.zh: 高懼，逃匿，終身不敢見詵。

translations.literal: Gao feared, fled and hid, and to the end of his life dared not see Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao hid and never again faced him.

sentences.zh: 興遣將鎮東楊佛嵩攻陷洛陽。

translations.literal: Xing sent the General Who Guards the East Yang Fosong to attack and capture Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing's general Yang Fosong took Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 班命郡國，百姓因荒自賣為奴婢者，悉免為良人。

translations.literal: He issued orders to commanderies and princedoms that commoners who because of famine had sold themselves as slaves or bondmaids were all freed to become free persons.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that anyone sold into slavery during the famine should be freed.

sentences.zh: 興以日月薄蝕，災眚屢見，降號稱王，下書令群公卿士將牧守宰各降一等。

translations.literal: Because sun and moon were eclipsed and disasters and prodigies repeatedly appeared, Xing lowered his title and styled himself king, issuing a document ordering dukes, ministers, gentlemen, generals, shepherds, guardians, and magistrates each to descend one grade.
translations.idiomatic: After eclipses and omens he demoted himself from emperor to king and cut every official's rank one step.

sentences.zh: 於是其太尉趙公旻等五十三人上疏諫曰：「伏惟陛下勳格皇天，功濟四海，威靈振於殊域，聲教暨于遐方，雖成湯之隆殷基，武王之崇周業，未足比喻。

translations.literal: Thereupon his Grand Commandant the Duke of Zhao Min and fifty-three others submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "We humbly consider that Your Majesty's merit matches august heaven, your work saves the four seas, your awesome spirit quakes distant regions, your transforming instruction reaches far lands—though Cheng Tang's raising Yin and King Wu's exalting Zhou are not enough for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-three ministers led by Zhao Min begged him to keep the throne, comparing him to Tang of Shang and Wu of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 方當廓靖江、吳，告成中嶽，豈宜過垂沖損，違皇天之眷命乎！

translations.literal: Just when you ought to clear the Yangzi and Wu and report completion at the central peak—how can it be fitting to humble yourself so far and go against bright heaven's favoring mandate!
translations.idiomatic: You mean to reunify the south and complete the sacred mountain rites—do not spurn heaven's mandate with false modesty!

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「殷湯、夏禹德冠百王，然猶順守謙沖，未居崇極，況朕寡昧，安可以處之哉！

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Tang of Yin and Yu of Xia in virtue capped the hundred kings, yet still observed modest restraint and did not occupy the supreme height—how much more I, dull and dim—how can I dwell there!
translations.idiomatic: "Yao Xing answered, "Even Tang and Yu stayed humble; I am far beneath them.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣旻告於社稷宗廟，大赦，改元弘始。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent Min to announce it at the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple, granted a great amnesty, and changed the era name to Hongshi.
translations.idiomatic: He had the demotion proclaimed at the shrines, amnestied the realm, and took the reign name Hongshi.

sentences.zh: 賜孤獨鰥寡栗帛有差，年七十已上加衣杖。

translations.literal: He granted grain and silk in graded amounts to orphans, widowers, and the childless; to those seventy years and above he added garments and staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He gave grain and cloth to the destitute and staffs to elders over seventy.

sentences.zh: 始平太守周班、槐里令李青彡皆以黷貨誅，於是郡國肅然矣。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Shiping Zhou Ban and the magistrate of Huaili Li Qingshan were both executed for taking bribes; thereupon commanderies and princedoms were sternly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ban and Li Qingshan died for corruption; the provinces took notice.

sentences.zh: 洛陽既陷，自淮、漢已北諸城，多請降送任。

translations.literal: After Luoyang had fallen, north of the Huai and Han most cities begged to surrender and sent hostages.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Huai and Han, cities offered hostages after Luoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 興下書聽祖父母昆弟得相容隱。

translations.literal: Xing issued a document permitting grandparents and elder brothers to shelter one another from prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed relatives to shield one another from criminal charges.

sentences.zh: 姚緒、姚碩德以興降號，固讓王爵，興弗許。

translations.literal: Yao Xu and Yao Shuode because Xing had lowered his title firmly declined princely rank; Xing did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xu and Yao Shuode tried to return their princely titles; Yao Xing refused.

sentences.zh: 京兆韋華、譙郡夏侯軌、始平龐眺等率襄陽流人一萬叛晉，奔於興。

translations.literal: Wei Hua of Jingzhao, Xiahou Gui of Qiao commandery, Pang Tiao of Shiping, and others led ten thousand Xiangyang refugees in revolt against Jin and fled to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua, Xiahou Gui, and Pang Tiao brought ten thousand refugees from Xiangyang to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興引見東堂，謂華曰：「晉自南遷，承平已久，今政化風俗何如？

translations.literal: Xing led them in audience at the east hall and said to Hua: "Since Jin moved south, peace has long reigned—how are government and custom now?
translations.idiomatic: At court he asked Wei Hua how the Eastern Jin fared.

sentences.zh: 」華曰：「晉主雖有南面之尊，無總禦之實，宰輔執政，政出多門，權去公家，遂成習俗，刑網峻急，風俗奢宕。

translations.literal: " Hua said: "Though the Jin lord has the honor of facing south, he has no reality of overall control; chief ministers hold power, policy issues from many gates, authority has left the ducal house, and it has become custom; the net of punishments is harsh and urgent, custom is extravagant and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: "Wei Hua said Jin's emperor was a figurehead: factions ruled, law grew harsh, and luxury spread.

sentences.zh: 自桓溫、謝安已後，未見寬猛之中。

translations.literal: From Huan Wen and Xie An onward, one has not seen the middle between lenient and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Since Huan Wen and Xie An, no ruler has balanced firm and mild rule.

sentences.zh: 」興大悅，拜華中書令。

translations.literal: " Xing was greatly pleased and appointed Hua Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing named him director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 興如河東。

translations.literal: Xing went to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時姚緒鎮河東，興待以家人之禮。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Xu garrisoned Hedong; Xing treated him with family courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He received Yao Xu with familial warmth.

sentences.zh: 下書封其先朝舊臣姚驢磑、趙惡地、王平、馬萬載、黃世等子為五等子男。

translations.literal: He issued a document enfeoffing the sons of former ministers of the prior court—Yao Luai, Zhao Edi, Wang Ping, Ma Wanzai, Huang Shi, and others—as sons and barons of the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled the heirs of old ministers such as Yao Luai and Zhao Edi.

sentences.zh: 命百僚舉殊才異行之士，刑政有不便於時者，皆除之。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend men of unusual talent and conduct, and whatever in punishments and government was inconvenient to the times—all was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He called for talent recommendations and scrapped bad laws.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎金城邊熙上陳軍令煩苛，宜遵簡約。

translations.literal: The gentleman of the Bureau of Military Affairs Bian Xi of Jincheng submitted that military orders were vexatious and harsh and ought to follow simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Xi urged simpler military regulations.

sentences.zh: 興覽而善之，乃依孫吳誓眾之法以損益之。

translations.literal: Xing read it and deemed it good; thereupon he followed Sun Wu's method of swearing in the host to adjust it.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing rewrote the code along Sun Wu's lines.

sentences.zh: 興立律學于長安，召郡縣散吏以授之。

translations.literal: Xing established a school of law at Chang'an and summoned scattered clerks of commanderies and counties to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a law academy in Chang'an for county clerks.

sentences.zh: 其通明者還之郡縣，論決刑獄。

translations.literal: Those who became clear in it were sent back to commanderies and counties to decide criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: Graduates returned home to try cases.

sentences.zh: 若州郡縣所不能決者，讞之廷尉。

translations.literal: What commanderies, princes, or counties could not decide was referred to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Unresolved suits went to the supreme judge.

sentences.zh: 興常臨諮議堂聽斷疑獄，于時號無冤滯。

translations.literal: Xing regularly attended the Deliberation Hall to hear and decide doubtful prisons; at the time he was called without wrongful delay.
translations.idiomatic: He heard appeals in person and was said to leave no innocent jailed.

sentences.zh: 姚緒、姚碩德固讓王爵，許之。

translations.literal: Yao Xu and Yao Shuode firmly declined princely rank; he permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: This time Yao Xing let them surrender princely titles.

sentences.zh: 緒、碩德威權日盛，興恐奸佞小人沮惑之，乃簡清正君子為之輔佐。

translations.literal: Xu and Shuode's awesome power grew daily; Xing feared crafty petty men would obstruct and bewilder them, and selected pure upright gentlemen to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing flatterers would taint his powerful uncles, he gave them honest advisers.

sentences.zh: 興以司隸校尉郭撫、扶風太守強超、長安令魚佩、槐里令彭明、倉部郎王年等清勤貞白，下書褒美，增撫邑一百戶，賜超爵關內侯，佩等進位一級。

translations.literal: Xing because Colonel Director of Retainers Guo Fu, Administrator of Fufeng Qiang Chao, magistrate of Chang'an Yu Pei, magistrate of Huaili Peng Ming, gentleman of the Granary Bureau Wang Nian, and others were pure, diligent, chaste, and white, issued a document praising them, increased Fu's fief by one hundred households, granted Chao noble rank within the passes, and advanced Pei and the others one grade.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Guo Fu, Qiang Chao, and other honest officials with titles and stipends.

sentences.zh: 使碩德率隴右諸軍伐乞伏乾歸，興潛軍赴之，乾歸敗走，降其部眾三萬六千，收鎧馬六萬匹。

translations.literal: He ordered Shuode to lead the various armies of Longyou to campaign against Qifu Gangui; Xing secretly marched to join him; Gangui was defeated and fled; he surrendered thirty-six thousand of his following and collected sixty thousand suits of armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode struck Qifu Gangui while Yao Xing reinforced him, taking thirty-six thousand prisoners and sixty thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 軍無私掠，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: The army engaged in no private plunder; the hundred surnames cherished them.
translations.idiomatic: His troops did not loot; the people loved them.

sentences.zh: 興進如枹罕，班賜王公以下，遍于卒伍。

translations.literal: Xing advanced to Fuhan, distributing rewards from princes and dukes downward even to the common soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuhan he rewarded every rank down to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 興之西也，沒奕於密欲乘虛襲安定，長史皇甫序切諫乃止。

translations.literal: When Xing went west, Moyuyu secretly wished to exploit the void to raid Anding; chief clerk Huangfu Xu remonstrated sharply and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Moyuyu meant to raid Anding while Yao Xing was away until Huangfu Xu stopped him.

sentences.zh: 于自恨失言，陰欲殺序。

translations.literal: Moyuyu privately resented having misspoken and secretly wished to kill Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Moyuyu brooded and plotted Huangfu Xu's murder.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸以窮蹙來降，拜鎮遠將軍、河州刺史、歸義侯，復以其部眾配之。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, pressed to extremity, came to surrender; he was appointed General Who Guards the Distance, Inspector of Hezhou, Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness, and his following was again assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The beaten Qifu Gangui submitted and was rearmed as inspector of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 興下書，將帥遭大喪，非在疆埸險要之所，皆聽奔赴，及期，乃從王役。

translations.literal: Xing issued a document that generals who met great bereavement, if not at critical points on the border, were all permitted to hurry home for burial, and when the term was fulfilled, then follow royal service.
translations.idiomatic: Generals could leave the front for parents' funerals unless posted at vital passes.

sentences.zh: 臨戎遭喪，聽假百日。

translations.literal: Those on campaign who met bereavement were permitted one hundred days' leave.
translations.idiomatic: Active officers got a hundred days' mourning leave.

sentences.zh: 若身為邊將，家有大變，交代未至，敢輒去者，以擅去官罪罪之。

translations.literal: If one was a frontier general and the household had a great change yet relief had not arrived, any who dared leave without order were punished for the crime of leaving office without authority.
translations.idiomatic: Border commanders who abandoned post without relief were prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 遣晉將軍劉嵩等二百三十七人歸於建鄴。

translations.literal: He sent Jin generals Liu Song and two hundred thirty-seven others back to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He repatriated 237 Jin captive officers to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 魏人襲沒奕于，於棄其部眾，率數千騎與赫連勃勃奔于秦州。

translations.literal: Wei troops raided Moyuyu; Moyuyu abandoned his following, led several thousand cavalry, and with Helian Bobo fled to Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked Moyuyu, who fled to Qinzhou with Helian Bobo.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進次瓦亭，長安大震，諸城閉門固守。

translations.literal: The Wei army advanced and halted at Wating; Chang'an was greatly shaken; the various cities closed gates and stubbornly defended.
translations.idiomatic: Wei reached Wating and threw Chang'an into panic; every gate shut.

sentences.zh: 魏平陽太守貳塵入侵河東。

translations.literal: Wei's Administrator of Pingyang Erchen invaded Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Erchen of Pingyang raided Hedong.

sentences.zh: 興於是練兵講武，大閱於城西，於勇壯異者召入殿中。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon drilled troops and discussed arms, held a great review west of the city, and summoned the brave and unusual into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing reviewed troops west of Chang'an and enrolled champions.

sentences.zh: 引見群臣於東堂，大議伐魏。

translations.literal: He led the host of ministers in audience at the east hall and greatly debated campaigning against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He debated war on Wei with his council.

sentences.zh: 群臣咸諫以為不可，興不從。

translations.literal: The host of ministers all remonstrated that it could not be done; Xing did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: All advised against it; he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 司隸姚顯進曰：「陛下天下之鎮，不宜親行，可使諸將分討，授以廟勝之策。

translations.literal: Colonel Director of Retainers Yao Xian advanced, saying: "Your Majesty is the realm's bulwark and ought not go in person; you may order the generals to divide and punish, granting them temple-victory stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xian urged him to stay home and delegate.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「王者正以廓土靖亂為務，吾焉得而辭之！」

translations.literal: " Xing said: "A king justly takes broadening territory and quieting chaos as his task—how can I decline it!"
translations.idiomatic: "A king must expand the realm and crush rebels," Yao Xing replied.

sentences.zh: 興立其子泓為皇太子，大赦境內，賜男子為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: Xing established his son Hong as crown prince, granted a general amnesty within his borders, and bestowed one noble rank on men who were heirs to fathers.
translations.idiomatic: He named Yao Hong heir and ennobled eldest sons.

sentences.zh: 遣姚平、狄伯支等率步騎四萬伐魏，姚碩德、姚穆率步騎六萬伐呂隆。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Ping, Di Bozhi, and others to lead forty thousand foot and horse against Wei, and Yao Shuode and Yao Mu to lead sixty thousand foot and horse against Lü Long.
translations.idiomatic: He launched Yao Ping at Wei and Yao Shuode at Lü Long.

sentences.zh: 平等軍次河東，興遣其光遠黨娥、立節雷星、建忠王多等率杏城及嶺北突騎自和寧赴援，越騎校尉唐小方、積弩姚良國率關中勁卒為平後繼，姚緒統河東見兵為前軍節度，姚紹率洛東之兵，姚詳率朔方見騎，並集平望，以會於興。

translations.literal: When Ping's army halted at Hedong, Xing sent his Guangyuan Dang E, Line-Establishing Lei Xing, Loyalty-Establishing Wang Duo, and others to lead Xingcheng and north-of-the-ranges shock cavalry from Hening to hurry as relief; Colonel of the Yue Cavalry Tang Xiaofang and Colonel of Accumulated Crossbows Yao Liangguo led crack troops of Guanzhong as Ping's rear; Yao Xu commanded Hedong's troops at hand as forward army director; Yao Shao led troops east of Luo; Yao Xiang led mounted men of Shuofang at hand—all assembled at Pingwang to join Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He staged a massive relief column for Yao Ping from Xingcheng, Guanzhong, Hedong, and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 使沒奕于權鎮上邽，中軍、廣陵公斂權鎮洛陽，姚顯及尚書令姚晃輔其太子泓，入直西宮。

translations.literal: He ordered Moyuyu provisionally to garrison Shanggui, the Central Army and Duke of Guangling Lian Quan to garrison Luoyang, Yao Xian and Director of the Secretariat Yao Huang to assist the crown prince Hong, entering duty at the west palace.
translations.idiomatic: Moyuyu held Shanggui, Lian Quan Luoyang, while Yao Xian and Yao Huang aided the heir in the west palace.

sentences.zh: 碩德至姑臧，大敗呂隆之眾，俘斬一萬。

translations.literal: Shuode reached Guzang and greatly defeated Lü Long's host, capturing and beheading ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode crushed Lü Long at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 隆將呂他等率眾二萬五千，以東苑來降。

translations.literal: Long's general Lü Ta and others led twenty-five thousand to surrender from the eastern park.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Ta brought twenty-five thousand men from the east garden.

sentences.zh: 先是，禿髮利鹿孤據西平，沮渠蒙遜據張掖，李玄盛據敦煌，與呂隆相持。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tufa Lugu had held Xiping, Juqu Mengsun held Zhangye, Li Xuansheng held Dunhuang, facing Lü Long.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Lugu, Juqu Mengsun, and Li Xuansheng had boxed in Lü Long.

sentences.zh: 至是，皆遣使降。

translations.literal: At this point all sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Now all three submitted.

sentences.zh: 興率戎卒四萬七千，自長安赴姚平。

translations.literal: Xing led forty-seven thousand tribal troops from Chang'an to hurry to Yao Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched forty-seven thousand men to Yao Ping.

sentences.zh: 平攻魏乾城，陷之，逐據柴壁。

translations.literal: Ping attacked Wei's Gancheng, captured it, and thereupon occupied Chaiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ping took Gancheng and Chaiyu.

sentences.zh: 魏軍大至，攻平，截汾水以守之。

translations.literal: The Wei host arrived in great force, attacked Ping, and cut off the Fen River to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei surrounded him and dammed the Fen.

sentences.zh: 興至蒲阪，憚而不進。

translations.literal: Xing reached Puyang, feared, and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing stopped cold at Puyang.

sentences.zh: 時碩德攻呂隆，撫納夷夏，分置守宰，節糧積粟，為持久之計。

translations.literal: At the time Shuode was attacking Lü Long, comforting and receiving Yi and Xia, dividing and setting guardians and magistrates, husbanding grain and accumulating millet, planning for a long stand.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yao Shuode was consolidating Liangzhou for a long siege of Lü Long.

sentences.zh: 隆懼，遂降。

translations.literal: Long feared and thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long capitulated.

sentences.zh: 碩德軍令齊整，秋毫無犯，祭先賢，禮儒哲，西土悅之。

translations.literal: Shuo De's military orders were orderly; not the slightest hair was violated; he sacrificed to former worthies and honored Confucian sages; the western lands rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode's discipline won the west: no looting, honors to sages.

sentences.zh: 姚平糧竭矢盡，將麾下三十騎赴汾水而死，狄伯支等十將四萬餘人，皆為魏所擒。

translations.literal: Yao Ping's grain was exhausted and arrows spent; he led thirty picked horsemen of his command toward the Fen River and died; Di Bozhi and ten other generals with more than forty thousand men were all captured by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ping drowned himself in the Fen; Di Bozhi and forty thousand men were taken.

sentences.zh: 興下書，軍士戰沒者，皆厚加褒贈。

translations.literal: Xing issued a document that soldiers who died in battle were all generously posthumously rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He enriched pensions for the Wei dead.

sentences.zh: 魏軍乘勝進攻蒲阪，姚緒固守不戰，魏乃引還。

translations.literal: The Wei army exploited victory to advance and attack Puyang; Yao Xu stubbornly defended and did not fight; Wei thereupon led away.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck Puyang but Yao Xu's defense drove them off.

sentences.zh: 興徙河西豪右萬餘戶于長安。

translations.literal: Xing moved more than ten thousand powerful households of Hexi to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He resettled ten thousand Hexi notables in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 晉輔國將軍袁虔之、甯朔將軍劉壽、冠軍將軍高長慶、龍驤將軍郭恭等貳于桓玄，懼而奔興。

translations.literal: Jin's General Who Supports the State Yuan Qianzhi, General Who Pacifies the North Liu Shou, General Who Vanquishes Gao Changqing, Dragon General Guo Gong, and others broke with Huan Xuan, feared, and fled to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Jin officers fleeing Huan Xuan sought Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興臨東堂引見，謂虔之等曰：「桓玄雖名晉臣，其實晉賊，其才度定何如父也？

translations.literal: Xing attended the east hall and led them in audience, saying to Qianzhi and others: "Though Huan Xuan bears the name of Jin minister, in truth he is Jin's bandit—how do his talents and measure compare with his father's?
translations.idiomatic: He asked them about Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 能辦成大事以不？

translations.literal: Can he accomplish a great affair or not?
translations.idiomatic: Could Huan Xuan finish what he started?

sentences.zh: 」虔之曰：「玄籍世資，雄據荊、楚，屬晉朝失政，遂偷竊宰衡。

translations.literal: " Qianzhi said: "Xuan relies on inherited capital, dominates Jing and Chu; because the Jin court lost government, he thereupon stole the chief minister's post.
translations.idiomatic: "Yuan Qianzhi called Huan Xuan a usurper holding Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 安忍無親，多忌好殺，位不才授，爵以愛加，無公平之度，不如其父遠矣。

translations.literal: He is cruel and bears no kin, jealous and fond of killing, offices not matched to talent, noble rank given by favor—there is no fairness; he is far inferior to his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was cruel, jealous, and nepotistic—nothing like his father.

sentences.zh: 今既握朝權，必行篡奪，既非命世之才，正可為他人驅除耳。

translations.literal: Now that he grips court power, he is sure to carry out usurpation; he is not a world-ordering talent—he can only clear the way for another.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing power without genius, he would only pave the way for a real founder.

sentences.zh: 此天以機便授之陛下，願速加經略，廓清吳、楚。

translations.literal: This is heaven lending opportunity to Your Majesty; I pray you speedily plan strategy and clear Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven offers you the south—strike quickly.

sentences.zh: 」興大悅，以虔之為大司農，餘皆有拜授。

translations.literal: " Xing was greatly pleased, made Qianzhi grand minister of agriculture, and the rest all received appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing made Yuan Qianzhi grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 虔之固讓，請疆埸自效，改授假節、甯南將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Qianzhi firmly declined, begging to show effort on the border, and was reappointed with false credentials General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianzhi took a southern frontier command instead.

sentences.zh: 興立其昭儀張氏為皇后，封子懿、弼、洸、宣、諶、愔、璞、質、逵、裕、國兒皆為公。

translations.literal: Xing established his Worthy Lady Zhang as empress and enfeoffed his sons Yi, Bi, Guang, Xuan, Chen, Yin, Pu, Zhi, Kui, Yu, and Guo'er all as dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Zhang empress and sons dukes.

sentences.zh: 遣其兼大鴻臚梁斐，以新平張構為副，拜禿髮傉檀車騎將軍、廣武公，沮渠蒙遜鎮西將軍、沙州刺史、西海侯，李玄盛安西將軍、高昌侯。

translations.literal: He sent his concurrent grand herald Liang Fei with Zhang Gou of Xinping as deputy to appoint Tufa Nutan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Duke of Guangwu, Juqu Mengsun General Who Guards the West, Inspector of Shazhou, and Marquis of Xihai, and Li Xuansheng General Who Pacifies the West and Marquis of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Tufa Nutan, Juqu Mengsun, and Li Xuansheng with Jin-style titles.

sentences.zh: 興遣鎮遠趙曜率眾二萬西屯金城，建節王松忿率騎助呂隆等守姑臧。

translations.literal: Xing sent General Who Guards the Distance Zhao Yao to lead twenty thousand west to garrison Jincheng, and General Who Establishes the Lineage Wang Songfen to lead cavalry to aid Lü Long and others in defending Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yao went to Jincheng; Wang Songfen rode to help Lü Long.

sentences.zh: 松忿至魏安，為傉檀弟文真所圍，眾潰，執松忿，送于傉檀。

translations.literal: Songfen reached Weian, was surrounded by Nutan's younger brother Wenzhen, scattered, was seized, and sent to Nutan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Songfen fell to Tufa Wenzhen and was sent to Nutan.

sentences.zh: 傉檀大怒，送松忿還長安，歸罪文真，深自陳謝。

translations.literal: Nutan was greatly angered, sent Songfen back to Chang'an, returned blame to Wenzhen, and deeply apologized himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Nutan returned the general and blamed his brother.

sentences.zh: 興下書，錄馬嵬戰時將吏，盡擢敘之，其堡戶給復二十年。

translations.literal: Xing issued a document recording officers and clerks of the Mawei battle, promoting them all; the fort households were granted exemption twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Mawei veterans and twenty years' tax relief for their forts.

sentences.zh: 興性儉約，車馬無金玉之飾，自下化之，莫不敦尚清素。

translations.literal: Xing's nature was frugal; carriages and horses had no jade or gold ornament; those below were transformed by him and none failed to honor purity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing lived plainly and set the tone for court austerity.

sentences.zh: 然好游田，頗損農要。

translations.literal: Yet he loved roaming and hunting, which somewhat harmed the essentials of farming.
translations.idiomatic: But he loved the hunt to the hurt of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 京兆杜挻以僕射齊難無匡輔之益，著《豐草詩》以箴之，馮翊相雲作《德獵賦》以諷焉。

translations.literal: Du Ting of Jingzhao, because Vice Director Qi Nan brought no benefit of support and correction, composed the poem 'Luxuriant Grass' to admonish him; Xiang Yun of Fengyi wrote the rite 'Virtue and the Hunt' to satirize him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ting and Xiang Yun wrote verse criticizing hunts and lax ministers.

sentences.zh: 興皆覽而善之，賜以金帛，然終弗能改。

translations.literal: Xing read them all and deemed them good, granted them gold and silk, yet to the end could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing praised their poems but kept hunting.

sentences.zh: 晉順陽太守彭泉以郡降興，興遣楊佛嵩率騎五千，與其荊州刺史趙曜迎之，遂寇陷南鄉，擒建威將軍劉嵩，略地至於梁國而歸。

translations.literal: Jin's Administrator of Shunyang Peng Quan surrendered his commandery to Xing; Xing sent Yang Fosong to lead five thousand cavalry with his Inspector of Jingzhou Zhao Yao to welcome him, thereupon raided and captured Nanxiang, seized General Who Establishes Might Liu Song, seized territory reaching Liang commandery, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Quan defected; Yang Fosong took Nanxiang and raided to Liang.

sentences.zh: 又遣其兼散騎常侍席確詣涼州，征呂隆弟超入侍，隆遣之。

translations.literal: He also sent his concurrent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Xi Que to Liangzhou to summon Lü Long's younger brother Chao to attend court; Long sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Que fetched Lü Chao as hostage.

sentences.zh: 呂隆懼禿髮傉檀之逼，表請內徙。

translations.literal: Lü Long feared Tufa Nutan's pressure and memorialized begging to move inward.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long asked to relocate inland before Tufa Nutan.

sentences.zh: 興遣齊難及鎮西姚詰、鎮遠乞伏乾歸、鎮遠趙曜等步騎四萬，迎隆於河西。

translations.literal: Xing sent Qi Nan together with General Who Guards the West Yao Jie, General Who Guards the Distance Qifu Gangui, General Who Guards the Distance Zhao Yao, and others, forty thousand foot and horse, to welcome Long west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan led forty thousand men to escort Lü Long east.

sentences.zh: 難至姑臧，以其司馬王尚行涼州刺史，配兵三千鎮姑臧，以將軍閻松為倉松太守，郭將為番禾太守，分戍二城，徙隆及其宗室僚屬于長安。

translations.literal: When Nan reached Guzang, he made his marshal Wang Shang acting Inspector of Liangzhou, assigned three thousand troops to garrison Guzang, made General Yan Song Administrator of Cangsong, Guo Jiang Administrator of Fanhe, divided garrisons between the two cities, and moved Long together with his lineage and staff to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan installed Wang Shang at Guzang and deported the Lü clan to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜遣弟如子貢其方物。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengsun sent his younger brother Ruzi to offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengsun sent tribute through his brother.

sentences.zh: 王尚綏撫遺黎，導以信義，百姓懷其惠化，翕然歸之。

translations.literal: Wang Shang comforted the remaining people, guided them with trust and righteousness; the hundred surnames cherished his kindly transformation and harmoniously submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang won Liangzhou with justice.

sentences.zh: 北部鮮卑並遣使貢款。

translations.literal: The northern Xianbei together sent envoys offering allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Northern tribes sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 桓玄遣使來聘，請辛恭靖、何澹之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan sent envoys on a friendly mission, asking for Xin Gongjing and He Danzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan asked for two captives back.

sentences.zh: 興留恭靖而遣澹之，謂曰：「桓玄不推計曆運，將圖篡逆，天未忘晉，必將有義舉，以吾觀之，終當傾覆。

translations.literal: Xing retained Gongjing and sent Danzhi, saying to him: "Huan Xuan does not reckon the calendar's turn and will plot usurpation; heaven has not forgotten Jin—there is sure to be a righteous rising; as I see it, he will in the end overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing kept Xin Gongjing and warned He Danzhi that Huan Xuan would fall.

sentences.zh: 卿今馳往，必逢其敗，相見之期，遲不雲遠。

translations.literal: If you hurry there now, you are sure to meet his defeat; the time we meet again is not far.
translations.idiomatic: He told He Danzhi he would soon see Huan Xuan's ruin.

sentences.zh: 」初，恭靖至長安，引見興而不拜，興曰：「朕將任卿以東南之事。

translations.literal: " Earlier, when Gongjing reached Chang'an, he was led in audience to Xing but did not bow; Xing said: "I am about to assign you to southeast affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xin Gongjing had refused to bow; Yao Xing had offered him office.

sentences.zh: 」靖曰：「我寧為國家鬼，不為羌賊臣。

translations.literal: " Jing said: "I would rather be a ghost for the state than a minister to Qiang bandits.
translations.idiomatic: "I will be Jin's ghost, not your minister," Xin replied.

sentences.zh: 」興怒，幽之別室。

translations.literal: " Xing was angry and imprisoned him in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing jailed him.

sentences.zh: 至是，恭靖亦逾牆遁歸。

translations.literal: At this point Gongjing also climbed the wall and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongjing then escaped over the wall.

sentences.zh: 興遣其將姚碩德、姚斂成、姚壽都等率眾三萬，伐楊盛于仇池。

translations.literal: Xing sent his generals Yao Shuode, Yao Liancheng, Yao Shoudou, and others to lead thirty thousand to campaign against Yang Sheng at Qiuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing dispatched Yao Shuode, Yao Liancheng, and Yao Shoudou with thirty thousand men against Yang Sheng.

sentences.zh: 壽都等入自宕昌，斂成從下辯而進。

translations.literal: Shoudou and others entered from Dangchang; Liancheng advanced from Xiabian.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shoudou came through Dangchang while Yao Liancheng moved up from Xiabian.

sentences.zh: 盛遣其弟壽距成，從子斌距都。

translations.literal: Sheng sent his younger brother Shou to oppose Cheng, and his nephew Bin to oppose Dou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng sent Yang Shou against Liancheng and nephew Yang Bin against Shoudou.

sentences.zh: 都逆擊擒之，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Dou met and struck them, captured them, and took all their host prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shoudou routed and captured them wholesale.

sentences.zh: 楊壽等懼，率眾請降。

translations.literal: Yang Shou and others feared and led the host begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou's party surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 碩德還師。

translations.literal: Shuo De returned the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuode withdrew.

sentences.zh: 晉汝南太守趙策委守奔於興。

translations.literal: Jin's Administrator of Runan Zhao Ce abandoned his post and fled to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ce of Runan defected to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 興如趙逍園，引諸沙門于澄玄堂聽鳩摩羅什演說佛經。

translations.literal: Xing went to Zhao Xiaoyuan's garden, led the various śramaṇas into the Clarify Mystery Hall, and listened to Kumārajīva expound Buddhist sūtras.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing heard Kumārajīva preach at the imperial cloister.

sentences.zh: 羅什通辯夏言，尋覽舊經，多有乘謬，不與胡本相應。

translations.literal: Roshi was fluent and eloquent in Chinese speech; when he surveyed old translations many carried errors and failed to match the Hu originals.
translations.idiomatic: Kumārajīva found earlier Chinese versions full of mistakes.

sentences.zh: 興與羅什及沙門僧略、僧遷、道樹、僧睿、道坦、僧肇、曇順等八百餘人，更出大品，羅什持胡本，興執舊經，以相考校，其新文異舊者皆會於理義。

translations.literal: Xing with Roshi and the śramaṇas Seng Lüe, Seng Qian, Dao Shu, Seng Rui, Dao Tan, Seng Zhao, Tan Shun, and more than eight hundred others newly produced the Great Perfection of Wisdom; Rosi held the Hu text, Xing held the old translation, and they collated them; wherever the new text differed from the old, all accorded with principle and meaning.
translations.idiomatic: With eight hundred monks Yao Xing retranslated the Great Perfection of Wisdom, comparing Kumārajīva's Sanskrit to old Chinese.

sentences.zh: 續出諸經並諸論三百餘卷。

translations.literal: They continued producing various sūtras and treatises, more than three hundred fascicles in all.
translations.idiomatic: They issued over three hundred further fascicles of scripture and śāstra.

sentences.zh: 今之新經皆羅什所譯。

translations.literal: Today's new scriptures are all translated by Roshi.
translations.idiomatic: The current canon is largely Kumārajīva's work.

sentences.zh: 興既托意於佛道，公卿已下莫不欽附，沙門自遠而至者五千餘人。

translations.literal: Since Xing had entrusted his aims to Buddhism and the Way, from dukes and ministers downward none failed to revere and attach themselves; śramaṇas who came from afar numbered more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside turned Buddhist; five thousand monks gathered at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 起浮圖於永貴裏，立波若台于中宮，沙門坐禪者恆有千數。

translations.literal: He raised a stūpa in Yonggui ward, set up a Prajñā terrace in the inner palace, and those śramaṇas who sat in meditation were constantly counted in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He built a stūpa and a prajñā platform; a thousand monks meditated daily.

sentences.zh: 州郡化之，事佛者十室而九矣。

translations.literal: Commanderies and princedoms were transformed by it; of those who served Buddha, nine houses in ten did so.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces followed: nine families in ten were Buddhist.

sentences.zh: 使姚碩德及冠軍徐洛生等伐仇池，又遣建武趙琨自宕昌而進，遣其將斂俱寇漢中。

translations.literal: He ordered Yao Shuode and the champion Xu Luosheng and others to campaign against Qiuqi, also sent General Who Establishes Might Zhao Kun to advance from Dangchang, and sent his general Lian Ju to raid Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He renewed the Qiuqi campaign and sent Lian Ju into Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時劉裕誅桓玄，迎復安帝，玄衛將軍、新安王桓謙，臨原王桓怡，雍州刺史桓蔚，左衛將軍桓謐，中書令桓胤，將軍何澹之等奔於興。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yu had executed Huan Xuan, welcomed and restored Emperor An; Xuan's Guard General and Prince of Xin'an Huan Qian, Prince of Linyuan Huan Yi, Inspector of Yongzhou Huan Wei, General of the Left Guard Huan Mi, Director of the Secretariat Huan Yin, General He Danzhi, and others fled to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's kinsmen and He Danzhi fled to Yao Xing after Liu Yu restored Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉裕遣大參軍衡凱之詣姚顯，請通和，顯遣吉默報之，自是聘使不絕。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent senior staff officer Heng Kaizhi to Yao Xian begging open peace; Xian sent Ji Mo to answer him; from this envoys on friendly missions were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu and Yao Xing exchanged peace envoys through Yao Xian.

sentences.zh: 晉求南鄉諸郡，興許之。

translations.literal: Jin begged the commanderies of Nanxiang; Xing granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin asked for Nanxiang; Yao Xing agreed.

sentences.zh: 群臣咸諫以為不可，興曰：「天下之善一也，劉裕拔萃起微，匡輔晉室，吾何惜數郡而不成其美乎！

translations.literal: The host of ministers all remonstrated that it could not be done; Xing said: "The good under heaven is one; Liu Yu, outstanding from humble beginnings, aids and supports the Jin house—why should I begrudge several commanderies and not complete his beauty!
translations.idiomatic: Ministers objected; Yao Xing said Liu Yu deserved the border towns.

sentences.zh: 」遂割南鄉、順陽、新野、舞陰等十二郡歸於晉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ceded Nanxiang, Shunyang, Xinye, Wuyin, and twelve other commanderies to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded twelve prefectures including Nanxiang and Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 姚碩德等頻敗楊盛，盛懼，請降，遣子難當及僚佐子弟數十人為質，碩德等引還。

translations.literal: Yao Shuode and others repeatedly defeated Yang Sheng; Sheng feared, begged to surrender, sent his son Nan Dang and several tens of sons and younger relatives of staff as hostages; Shuode and others led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng submitted hostages after repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 署盛為使持節、散騎常侍、都督益、甯州諸軍事、征南大將軍、開府、益州牧、武都侯。

translations.literal: He appointed Sheng Bearer of the Imperial Insignia, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Yi and Ning, Grand General Who Conquers the South, privilege of opening a general's office, Governor of Yi, and Marquis of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng received full honors as governor of Yi and marquis of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 斂俱陷城固，徙漢中流人郭陶等三千餘家於關中。

translations.literal: Lian Ju captured Chenggu and moved more than three thousand refugee households of Guo Tao and others from Hanzhong to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Ju took Chenggu and deported three thousand Hanzhong families.

sentences.zh: 興班告境內及在朝文武，立名不得犯叔父緒及碩德之名，以彰殊禮。

translations.literal: Xing issued a proclamation to the borders and to civil and military officials at court that established names must not offend against the names of his uncles Xu and Shuo De, thereby displaying special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade personal names that clashed with his uncles Yao Xu and Yao Shuode.

sentences.zh: 興謙恭孝友，每見緒及碩德，如家人之禮，整服傾悚，言則稱字，車馬服玩，必先二叔，然後服其次者，朝廷大政，必諮之而後行。

translations.literal: Xing was modest, respectful, filial, and fraternal; whenever he saw Xu and Shuo De it was with family courtesy—he set his robes straight and stood in awe, in speech used their style names, and with carriages, horses, garments, and playthings always presented to the two uncles first, then used what came after; on great policies of court he always consulted them before acting.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his uncles like elders, gave them first pick of gifts, and sought their counsel on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 太史令郭黁言於興曰：「戌亥之歲，當有孤寇起於西北，宜慎其鋒。

translations.literal: Astrologer Director Guo Nen spoke to Xing, saying: "In the years of Xu and Hai a lone bandit will arise in the northwest—you should beware his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen prophesied northwest trouble in Xu-Hai years.

sentences.zh: 起兵如流沙，死者如亂麻，戎馬悠悠會隴頭，鮮卑、烏丸居不安，國朝疲於奔命矣。

translations.literal: Armies rise like shifting sand, dead like tangled hemp; warhorses will long gather at Longtou; Xianbei and Wuhuan will not dwell in peace; the dynasty will tire itself rushing to commands.
translations.idiomatic: His rhyme foretold border chaos and Xianbei unrest.

sentences.zh: 」時所在有泉水湧出，傳云飲則愈病，後多無驗。

translations.literal: " At the time everywhere springs gushed forth; rumor said drinking them cured illness; afterward mostly there was no verification.
translations.idiomatic: Healing springs appeared then proved false.

sentences.zh: 屢有妖人自稱神女，戮之乃止。

translations.literal: Repeatedly there were uncanny persons styling themselves spirit maidens; when slain they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: False prophetesses were executed.

sentences.zh: 興大閱，自杜郵至於羊牧。

translations.literal: Xing held a great review from Duyou to Yangmu.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed troops from Duyou to Yangmu.

sentences.zh: 興以姚碩德來朝，大赦其境內。

translations.literal: Because Yao Shuode came to court, Xing granted a great amnesty within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied the realm when Yao Shuode visited.

sentences.zh: 及碩德歸於秦州，興送之，及雍乃還。

translations.literal: When Shuode returned to Qinzhou, Xing escorted him and only turned back at Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing escorted his uncle to Yong.

sentences.zh: 禿髮傉檀獻興馬三千匹，羊三萬頭。

translations.literal: Tufa Nutan presented Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Nutan sent three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 興以為忠於己，乃署傉檀為涼州刺史，征涼州刺史王尚還長安。

translations.literal: Xing thought him loyal to himself and thereupon appointed Nutan Inspector of Liangzhou, summoning Inspector of Liangzhou Wang Shang back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking it loyalty, Yao Xing swapped Wang Shang for Tufa Nutan as governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 涼州人申屠英等二百餘人，遣主簿胡威詣興，請留尚，興弗許。

translations.literal: More than two hundred men of Liangzhou such as Shentu Ying sent chief clerk Hu Wei to Xing begging to retain Shang; Xing did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred Liangzhou notables begged to keep Wang Shang; Yao Xing refused.

sentences.zh: 引威見之，威流涕謂興曰：「臣州奉國五年，王威不接，銜膽棲冰、孤城獨守者，仰恃陛下威靈，俯杖良牧惠化。

translations.literal: He led Wei in audience; Wei wept and said to Xing: "My province has served the state five years without royal majesty drawing near; those who hold gall and dwell on ice, alone guarding a solitary city, look up relying on Your Majesty's awesome spirit and look down leaning on a good shepherd's kindly transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Wei wept that Liangzhou had served faithfully under Wang Shang.

sentences.zh: 忽違天人之心，以華土資狄。

translations.literal: Suddenly to go against the hearts of heaven and men and with Chinese soil aid the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Now you hand Chinese land to barbarians.

sentences.zh: 若傉檀才望應代，臣豈敢言。

translations.literal: If Nutan's talent and reputation fitted succession, how would your subject dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: If Tufa Nutan were fit to rule, I would be silent.

sentences.zh: 竊聞乃以臣等貿馬三千匹，羊三萬口，如所傳實者，是為棄人貴畜。

translations.literal: Privately I hear it is because you traded us for three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep—if the rumor is true, this is discarding men and prizing beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor says you sold us for livestock—that values animals over people.

sentences.zh: 苟以馬供軍國，直煩尚書一符，三千餘家戶輸一匹，朝下夕辦，何故以一方委此奸胡！

translations.literal: If horses were wanted for army and state, it would suffice for the secretariat to issue one tally and more than three thousand households each render one hide—morning order, evening done—why entrust a whole region to this treacherous Hu!
translations.idiomatic: A requisition could raise the horses; why give a province to aliens?

sentences.zh: 昔漢武傾天下之資，開建河西，隔絕諸戎，斷匈奴右臂，所以終能屠大宛王毋寡。

translations.literal: In the past Han Wu tilted the realm's resources to open Hexi, cut off the various Rong, severed the Xiongnu' right arm—therefore in the end he could slaughter the King of Dayuan, Wu Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu built Hexi to break the Xiongnu and take Dayuan.

sentences.zh: 今陛下方布政玉門，流化西域，奈何以五郡之地資之犬嚴狁，忠誠華族棄之虐虜！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is just spreading government at Jade Gate, extending transformation to the Western Regions—how can you with the land of five commanderies aid these dog Xianyun and cast off loyal Chinese clans to cruel captives!
translations.idiomatic: You mean to civilize the west yet you feed five commanderies to Xianyun and abandon Chinese loyalty!

sentences.zh: 非但臣州裏塗炭，懼方為聖朝旰食之憂。

translations.literal: It is not only that my province will be smeared with mud and charcoal—I fear it will become the sagely court's worry of eating only at noon and night.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou will burn and the court will pay.

sentences.zh: 」興乃遣西平人車普馳止王尚，又遣使喻傉檀。

translations.literal: " Xing thereupon sent Che Pu of Xiping in haste to stop Wang Shang, and also sent envoys to instruct Nutan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Che Pu to recall Wang Shang and wrote Tufa Nutan.

sentences.zh: 會傉檀已至姑臧，普以狀先告之。

translations.literal: It happened that Nutan had already reached Guzang; Pu reported the situation to him first.
translations.idiomatic: Che Pu met Tufa Nutan already at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 傉檀懼，脅遣王尚，遂入姑臧。

translations.literal: Nutan feared, coerced Shang's departure, and thereupon entered Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Nutan forced Wang Shang out and took Guzang.

sentences.zh: 尚既至長安，坐匿呂氏宮人，擅殺逃人薄禾等，禁止南台。

translations.literal: When Shang reached Chang'an, for concealing palace women of the Lü clan and on his own authority killing fugitives Bo He and others, he was confined at the south terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang was jailed for hiding Lü concubines and killing fugitives.

sentences.zh: 涼州別駕宗敞、治中張穆、主簿邊憲、胡威等上疏理尚曰：

translations.literal: The Liangzhou aide-de-camp Zong Chang, administrator Zhang Mu, chief clerks Bian Xian, Hu Wei, and others submitted a memorial defending Shang, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chang, Zhang Mu, Bian Xian, and Hu Wei petitioned for Wang Shang:

sentences.zh: 臣州荒裔，鄰帶寇仇，居泰無垂拱之安，運否離傾覆之難。

translations.literal: Our province is a remote border, neighboring bandit foes; in peace it lacks the security of folded hands, in ill fortune it suffers the hardship of overturning.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou is a frontier ever under threat.

sentences.zh: 自張氏頹基，德風絕而莫扇；

translations.literal: From the Zhang house's fallen foundation, virtuous wind ceased and none fanned it;
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhangs fell, virtue died;

sentences.zh: 呂數將終，梟鶚以之翻翔。

translations.literal: as the Lü reckoning neared its end, owls and kites wheeled on the wing.
translations.idiomatic: the Lü regime rotted while predators circled.

sentences.zh: 群生嬰罔極之痛，西夏有焚如之禍。

translations.literal: The masses met boundless pain; the western Xia knew disaster like burning.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered; the west was fire.

sentences.zh: 幸皇鑒降眷，純風遠被。

translations.literal: Fortunately imperial regard descended in favor; pure wind spread from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace reached us like a cleansing wind.

sentences.zh: 刺史王尚受任垂滅之州，策成難全之際，輕身率下，躬儉節用，勞逸豐約，與眾同之，勸課農桑，時無廢業。

translations.literal: Inspector Wang Shang received appointment in a province on the verge of extinction, forged success in a moment hard to preserve; with light person he led those below, personally was frugal and restrained in use, in toil and ease, plenty and want, shared with the multitude, urged farming and sericulture, and seasons knew no abandoned work.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang took a dying province, lived simply, shared hardship, and restored farming.

sentences.zh: 然後振王威以掃不庭，回天波以蕩氛穢。

translations.literal: Then he roused royal majesty to sweep the unsubmissive, turned heaven's wave to wash away foul miasma.
translations.idiomatic: Then he struck rebels and cleared the land.

sentences.zh: 則群逆冰摧，不俟硃陽之曜；

translations.literal: Then the pack of rebels shattered like ice without waiting for the red sun's blaze;
translations.idiomatic: Rebels melted like frost;

sentences.zh: 若秋霜隕籜，豈待勁風之威。

translations.literal: like autumn frost felling bamboo leaves—how could it wait for fierce wind's might.
translations.idiomatic: they fell like leaves—no need of gale.

sentences.zh: 何定遠之足高，營平之獨美！

translations.literal: How He Dingyuan alone was lofty, Ying Ping alone beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: What need of famous generals of old?

sentences.zh: 經始甫爾，會朝算改授，使希世之功不終於必成，易失之機踐之而莫展。

translations.literal: The work had barely begun when court calculation changed appointment, making a world-rare merit not reach its sure completion and a easily lost opportunity trodden without unfolding.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he succeeded, you recalled him and wasted his work.

sentences.zh: 當其時而明其事者，誰不慨然！

translations.literal: Those who at that time understood the affair—who did not sigh bitterly!
translations.idiomatic: Who could not grieve?

sentences.zh: 既遠役遐方，劬勞於外，雖效未酬恩，而在公無闕。

translations.literal: Already far laboring on a distant frontier, toiling outside—though the effect did not yet repay favor, in public duty there was no fault.
translations.idiomatic: He served abroad without fault though reward was thin.

sentences.zh: 自至京師，二旬於今，出車之命莫逮，萋斐之責惟深。

translations.literal: Since reaching the capital, twenty days until now—the order for his carriage has not come; blame for slander runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days in Chang'an—no summons, only slander.

sentences.zh: 以取呂氏宮人裴氏及殺逃人薄禾等為南台所禁，天鑒玄鏡，暫免圇圄，譏繩之文，未離簡墨。

translations.literal: Because he took Lü clan palace woman Pei and killed fugitives Bo He and others he was confined by the south terrace—heaven's mirror for the moment spared prison, yet calumny's cords have not left the inked bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: South terrace jailed him for Pei and Bo He though heaven knows better.

sentences.zh: 裴氏年垂知命，首發二毛，嫠居本家，不在尚室，年邁姿陋，何用送為！

translations.literal: Lady Pei's years approach knowing heaven's mandate; her hair first shows two locks; widowed she dwells in her own family, not in Shang's chamber; advanced in years, plain in looks—what use sending her off!
translations.idiomatic: Pei is an old widow in her own home—no concubine of Wang Shang.

sentences.zh: 邊籓耍捍，眾力是寄，禾等私逃，罪應憲墨，以殺止殺，安邊之義也。

translations.literal: The frontier barrier needs defense; many shoulders bear the load; He and others fled privately, guilt fitting the inked forehead—to kill to stop killing is the meaning of pacifying the border.
translations.idiomatic: Bo He was a deserter; killing him secured the border.

sentences.zh: 假若以不送裴氏為罪者，正闕奚官之一女子耳。

translations.literal: Suppose not sending off Lady Pei were a crime—it lacks only one palace woman of the Xiguan office.
translations.idiomatic: At worst one palace maid is missing.

sentences.zh: 論勳則功重，言瑕則過微。

translations.literal: Measured for merit the work is weighty; spoken for blemish the fault is slight.
translations.idiomatic: His service outweighs petty faults.

sentences.zh: 而執憲吹毛求疵，忘勞記過，斯先哲所以泣血于當年，微臣所以仰天而灑淚。

translations.literal: Yet those who wield the law blow hairs seeking flaws, forget toil and record faults—this is why former sages wept blood in their years and why your petty servant looks up to heaven and sprinkles tears.
translations.idiomatic: Judges nitpick and forget his labor—sages wept for less.

sentences.zh: 且尚之奉國，曆事二朝，能否效於既往，優劣簡在聖心，就有微過，功足相補，宜弘罔極之施，以彰覆載之恩。

translations.literal: Moreover Shang's service to the state has spanned two courts; ability and inability show in the past, good and bad are sifted in the sagely mind—even if there were slight faults, merit is enough to offset them; you ought to extend boundless grace and display the kindness that covers and carries.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang served two regimes; pardon small slips for great deeds.

sentences.zh: 臣等生自西州，無翰飛之翼，久沈偽政，絕進趣之途。

translations.literal: We your subjects were born in the western province without wings to fly to Han; long sunk in false government, cut off from paths of advancement.
translations.idiomatic: We westerners had no path under past tyrants.

sentences.zh: 及皇化既沾，投竿之心冥發，遂策名委質，位忝吏端。

translations.literal: When imperial transformation had moistened us, the heart to cast aside the pole awoke in darkness; thereupon we inscribed names and entrusted substance, disgracing the clerks' end.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue let us take office.

sentences.zh: 主辱臣憂，故重繭披款，惟陛下亮之。

translations.literal: The lord humiliated, the minister grieves—therefore we double our soles and lay bare sincerity; only may Your Majesty enlighten it.
translations.idiomatic: We come with heavy hearts—hear us.

sentences.zh: 興覽之大悅，謂其黃門侍郎姚文祖曰：「卿知宗敞乎？

translations.literal: Xing read it and was greatly pleased, saying to his Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Yao Wenzu: "Do you know Zong Chang?
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing asked Yao Wenzu about Zong Chang.

sentences.zh: 」文祖曰：「與臣州裏，西方之英雋。

translations.literal: " Wenzu said: "He is of my province; a splendid talent of the west.
translations.idiomatic: "He is our countryman and a western star.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「有表理王尚，文義甚佳，當王尚研思耳。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "There is a memorial reasoning Wang Shang; the literary sense is very fine—it must be Wang Shang's polished thought.
translations.idiomatic: "This petition for Wang Shang is brilliant—Wang Shang must have drafted it.

sentences.zh: 」文祖曰：「尚在南台，禁止不與賓客交通，敞寓於楊桓，非尚明矣。

translations.literal: " Wenzu said: "Shang is at the south terrace, forbidden to traffic with guests; Chang lodges with Yang Huan—not Shang is clear.
translations.idiomatic: "Wang Shang is incommunicado; Zong Chang stays with Yang Huan—so Wang did not write it.

sentences.zh: 」興曰：「若爾，桓為措思乎？

translations.literal: " Xing said: "If so, did Huan set the thought?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Huan then?

sentences.zh: 」文祖曰：「西方評敞甚重，優於楊桓。

translations.literal: " Wenzu said: "The west ranks Chang very high, above Yang Huan.
translations.idiomatic: "The west esteems Zong Chang above Yang Huan.

sentences.zh: 敞昔與呂超周旋，陛下試可問之。

translations.literal: Chang formerly circled with Lü Chao—Your Majesty may try asking him.
translations.idiomatic: Ask Lü Chao—he knew Zong Chang.

sentences.zh: 」興因謂超曰：「宗敞文才何如？

translations.literal: " Xing thereupon said to Chao: "How is Zong Chang's literary talent?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Lü Chao how good Zong Chang was.

sentences.zh: 可是誰輩？

translations.literal: To what company does he belong?
translations.idiomatic: Who is his peer?

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「敞在西土，時論甚美，方敞魏之陳、徐，晉之潘、陸。

translations.literal: " Chao said: "In the western lands contemporary opinion esteems him greatly; he matches Chen and Xu of Wei, Pan and Lu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: "Zong Chang ranks with Chen Lin, Xu Gan, Pan Yue, and Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 」即以表示超曰：「涼州小地，寧有此才乎？

translations.literal: " Thereupon he showed the memorial to Chao, saying: "Can a small land like Liangzhou have such talent?
translations.idiomatic: He showed the memorial: could Liangzhou produce this?

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「臣以敞余文比之，未足稱多。

translations.literal: " Chao said: "Your subject comparing Chang's remaining writings—this does not count as much.
translations.idiomatic: "Compared to his other work this is ordinary.

sentences.zh: 琳琅出於昆嶺，明珠生於海濱，若必以地求人，則文命大夏之棄夫，姬昌東夷之擯士。

translations.literal: Fine jade comes from Kun range, bright pearls from the sea shore—if you must seek men by locality, then Wenming was a cast-off man of great Xia, Jichang a rejected scholar of eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Genius is not geography—Yu and Wen Wang came from humble ground.

sentences.zh: 但當問其文彩何如，不可以區宇格物。

translations.literal: You should only ask how the literary color is; you cannot use region to measure things.
translations.idiomatic: Judge the prose, not the map.

sentences.zh: 」興悅，赦尚之罪，以為尚書。

translations.literal: " Xing was pleased, pardoned Shang's crime, and made him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing freed Wang Shang and named him director of the secretariat.
